prompt: A restaurant owner says: 'I want an app so customers can order food.' They have one location, a small budget and most orders come from regulars who already visit their website.

task.prompt: A restaurant owner says: 'I want an app so customers can order food.' They have one location, a small budget and most orders come from regulars who already visit their website.

steps.question: What is the most sensible first suggestion to explore?
options: A desktop application
A blockchain loyalty platform
A mobile-friendly web ordering page on their existing site
Native iOS and Android apps plus a custom AI recommendation engine
steps.explanation: A responsive web page reaches customers without app-store downloads and fits a small budget.

steps.question: The owner later wants push notifications for daily specials and a loyalty card on the phone. What changes?
options: A mobile app (often cross-platform) becomes worth discussing, since those features suit apps
Nothing; websites do everything apps do
They need a separate desktop app
They must hire an in-house AI team
steps.explanation: Push notifications and on-device loyalty are strengths of mobile apps, so the case for one gets stronger.

prompt: Rank these client needs by how strongly they point to a native or cross-platform mobile app rather than a web app, strongest first.

task.prompt: Rank these client needs by how strongly they point to a native or cross-platform mobile app rather than a web app, strongest first.

items.label: A marketing site that should rank on Google
An internal admin dashboard used on office desktops
Field workers must capture photos and GPS location offline in areas with no signal
Customers want reminders through push notifications

task.explanation: Offline device features are the strongest reason for mobile; push is strong; SEO and desktop admin work point to web.

prompt: A new BD rep wrote these notes explaining product types to a client. Mark the incorrect statements.

task.prompt: A new BD rep wrote these notes explaining product types to a client. Mark the incorrect statements.

segments.text: A web app runs in the browser, so users do not need to install anything.
Native mobile apps are built separately for iOS and Android.
Cross-platform frameworks like React Native or Flutter let one codebase target both iOS and Android.
A web app can never work on a phone.
segments.issue: Responsive web apps work well on phones; they just cannot use every device feature.

segments.text: An AI feature means the app needs no human review, ever.
segments.issue: AI output can be wrong; most products need review, guardrails or fallbacks.

segments.text: Mobile apps usually need app-store review before each release.

prompt: A logistics client wants an 'AI app' that reads delivery notes (photos of handwritten slips) and fills in their order system.

task.prompt: A logistics client wants an 'AI app' that reads delivery notes (photos of handwritten slips) and fills in their order system.

steps.question: What is the most important question to ask first?
options: What colour should the app be?
Can we skip testing to launch faster?
What samples of slips exist, and how accurate does extraction need to be before it saves time?
Which AI model is the newest?
steps.explanation: AI feasibility depends on real data and an agreed accuracy bar; model choice comes later.

steps.question: They say about 10% of slips are barely readable. What should the solution include?
options: A review screen where staff check low-confidence results before they enter the system
Nothing; the AI will learn to read them automatically
Reject the project
Promise 100% accuracy
steps.explanation: A human-in-the-loop step for low-confidence cases keeps bad data out while still saving time.

steps.question: How should you describe ongoing costs to the client?
options: Only hosting costs a fixed small amount forever
Costs only go down over time automatically
Besides build cost, AI usage costs scale with the number of slips processed, plus monitoring and maintenance
There are no ongoing costs once it is built
steps.explanation: AI features usually carry per-use model costs and need monitoring; clients should hear that upfront.

prompt: A client has a fixed budget and wants to reach both iPhone and Android users quickly. Rank these approaches by fit, best first.

task.prompt: A client has a fixed budget and wants to reach both iPhone and Android users quickly. Rank these approaches by fit, best first.

items.label: Two separate native apps built in parallel
One cross-platform app (e.g. Flutter or React Native) for both platforms
A responsive web app first, mobile app later

task.explanation: Cross-platform covers both stores with one codebase; a web app is a cheaper reach option without store presence; two native apps cost the most; iOS-only misses Android users.

prompt: Mark the overpromises in this proposal paragraph about an AI support chatbot.

task.prompt: Mark the overpromises in this proposal paragraph about an AI support chatbot.

segments.text: The chatbot will answer common questions using your help-centre articles.
It will never give a wrong answer.
segments.issue: No AI system can guarantee this; promise guardrails and escalation instead.

segments.text: Questions it cannot answer confidently are handed to a human agent.
It will replace your entire support team in month one.
segments.issue: Unrealistic and alarming; position it as reducing repetitive tickets.

segments.text: We will review accuracy with your team weekly during the first month.

prompt: What is a key advantage of a web app over a mobile app for a new product?

options: It never needs updates
Users can open it from a link without installing anything
It can always work fully offline
It gets automatic access to every phone sensor
mcq.explanation: No install lowers the barrier to try a product. Offline use and full device access are strengths of native apps.

prompt: A client asks what 'cross-platform' means. Which explanation is best?

options: Two teams build two separate apps
One codebase builds apps for both iOS and Android
The app runs only in a web browser
The app works only on tablets
mcq.explanation: Cross-platform frameworks share most code across iOS and Android, saving time and cost.

prompt: A client wants an AI feature that summarises customer reviews. What should BD make clear early?

options: Output quality depends on their data, and there are ongoing usage costs and review needs
AI features are free to run once built
The summaries will always be perfect
No data is needed
mcq.explanation: Data, accuracy expectations and running costs are what make AI projects succeed or disappoint.
